registry_info.name: chapter_arc
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `chapter` family (chaos - noise - pattern - emergence - evolution). Five stations on one rail, all five reading the same hundred draws, so the arc the randomness sequence teaches is a spatial fact rather than a ten-second timer.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The five station names and ELITE_FRACTION are PRELOADED from extrem_randomness.gd at runtime and validated at _ready in both directions; the evidence ladder is preloaded from noise_quarry.gd the same way. Do not retype either here or in the script.

chapter_arc.name: Chapter Arc
chapter_arc.description: The five chapters of the randomness book standing along one rail at once. chaos, noise, pattern, emergence and evolution are the arc that sequence teaches in order — unstructured draw, then correlation, then rule, then organisation, then selection — and every artifact that carries them shows ONE at a time, with `all` reserved for a ten-second timer no still photograph can hold. Here all five stand along +x, each reading the SAME hundred draws through its own rule, so the progression is a spatial fact instead of a claim in a document. `steps` is how many times each station has applied its rule: at 0 the five stations are five copies of one scatter, which is the common origin the parent never had, and at 60 they are five silhouettes that the rules and not the staging produced. `evidence` is how much proof is standing that they were handed the same numbers — nothing, the shared draw's own footprint under each station with a carry ribbon from where each tenth body started, or a counted census of every station on one fixed gauge. The census is where the artifact disagrees with the curriculum. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random.
interactions: stand at the left end and look along the rail: the five clouds are the same hundred numbers, five rules deep
find one body's carry ribbon at the evolution station and follow it back to where that body started — the same point at all five stations
read the spread row on the board: the first three bars are the same bar, and that is the finding
set steps to 0 and the arc becomes five copies of one scatter — the common origin the parent's five chapters never share
count the gold bodies at the evolution station: ten of a hundred, which is ELITE_FRACTION read out of the parent's own const
chapter_arc.qfep_connection: A curriculum is an order imposed on things that do not carry it, and the only way to find out whether the order is real is to put the things side by side on one draw and measure. Done here, the ladder that the randomness sequence teaches turns out not to be a ladder of constraint at all for its first three rungs: chaos, noise and pattern leave the spread of the draw exactly where they found it and change only its texture. The progression is still true — each rule reads more than the last — but the thing it progresses in is not the thing the word 'constraint' promises. The arc is built so that this can be seen rather than argued, and so that it could have come out the other way.
chapter_arc.relationships: Synthesised from the six registry names that declare `chapter` over two scenes: extreme_randomness and its four .tscn wrappers particle_randomness_pure / _perlin / _patterns / _emergent, which are one script under five names, plus facade_grammar_demo, which carries the word against an architectural value list. Replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside: those five can each show ONE chapter and this shows all five at once, which is the value of the word they all declare and cannot photograph. Reads the five station names and ELITE_FRACTION out of extrem_randomness.gd's own consts and the evidence ladder out of noise_quarry.gd's, so three synthesis artifacts share one vocabulary. Sibling in form to noise_quarry (one field cut three ways) and generator_bench (one cut filled four ways); this is one DRAW read five ways.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 7.70 m across the five bays by 1.16 m deep, with the board standing 0.62 m behind it and 1.72 m up. It wants to be walked ALONG rather than approached: the whole argument is the left-to-right reading, so a placement that puts a wall or another artifact at either end costs the exhibit its first or last chapter.
spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 7.70 m, h 1.72 m, registry.measurements)

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the same geometry driven by the same LCG; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts: the apron, five bays, five body meshes, up to five carry meshes, up to forty origin-frame slabs, two board halves and up to ten census bars. The five Label3D tabs are not counted by that function and sit inside the box in any case.

dna.axis_shape:
THE FAMILY WORD IS EXHIBITED, NOT SWEPT, AND SO IS ITS FIRST VALUE — and the evidence for both is in extrem_randomness.gd rather than in its prose.

`chapter` SITS SIDE BY SIDE. The word is declared by six registry names over two scenes: five of them (extreme_randomness, particle_randomness_pure / _perlin / _patterns / _emergent) against ONE script, extrem_randomness.gd, carrying all | chaos | noise | pattern | emergence | evolution; the sixth, facade_grammar_demo, carries an architectural list sharing only the word and the leading `all`. In the script the five named values are spent by two flat five-branch dispatches — `match current_demo` at :253-258 over the update rules and `match demo_index` at :271-286 over the stagings — and the five rules are five functions (:301, :330, :360, :400, :469) not one of which calls another. No branch contains another. No value is another value plus a term: a flock is not a random walk with a term added, and a ranking is not a flock with a term added. Parallel values are exactly the case where holding them all at once is NOT merely the top value — it is the object — so the five stand together in every one of the nine tiles, lettered on the apron, and the axes vary something else.

BUT THE ARGUMENT NESTS, WHICH IS WHY THIS ARTIFACT EXISTS. The parent's own doc block (:22-35) reads the five as a ladder in which each rule reads everything the previous one read plus one more source: chaos reads nothing (three fresh draws per body per step, :307), noise reads POSITION (:337-339), pattern reads position under an EQUATION (:368-383), emergence reads every OTHER body (:421-433), evolution reads a RANKING of every other body against a target (:515-522). So the CODE is parallel and the CLAIM is nested — the MIXED case — and until now nothing in the corpus could test the claim, because a body can only run one rule at a time and no artifact could stand two of the five at once.

`evidence` NESTS in the ordinary way: result is contained in trace is contained in longhand. _build() adds the origin frames and the carry ribbons under `if evidence == "trace" or evidence == "longhand"` and the census under `if evidence == "longhand"`; no rung removes a mark an earlier rung drew, and the five station clouds are identical at all three. Its tail is a ceiling, not a case.

`steps` NESTS more literally than a ladder usually does: the k-step state is a PREFIX of the k+1-step trajectory, because _read_stations() applies the same function one more time to the state the previous rung ended in. Nothing is re-drawn and no rule changes. The one thing that is not nested is the evolution station's ranking, which is recomputed every step from the positions at the start of that step — that is the parent's own behaviour (:515) and not an artefact of this build.

WHY `all` IS EXHIBITED RATHER THAN KEPT AS A VALUE, which is the question the brief asks. In extrem_randomness.gd `all` is the value that pins nothing: _chapter_demo_index() (:598) finds no match for it in CHAPTER_DEMOS, returns -1, and _ready leaves display_time at its shipped 10.0, so the book turns its own pages on a timer. extreme_randomness's own dna.default says the consequence out loud — at a pinned chapter 0 the code freezes rather than restages, "so 'all' and 'chaos' are the same picture". A STILL CANNOT PHOTOGRAPH `all`. It is a union over TIME, and the evidence in this project is one PNG per value, so of the six declared values exactly five have ever been photographable and the sixth has only ever been photographed as the first.

This arc is that union taken out of time and laid along +x, which makes it a permanent, spatial `chapter = all`. Keeping `all` as a value would mean five of six variants were the arc refusing to be an arc — five worse copies of five artifacts that already ship, each with four empty bays beside it. The word is spent by the object. (disclosure_cabinet's nesting question, answered the other way round: there the cabinet could stand inside its own top rung; here the strip IS the rung.)
dna.default:
evidence=longhand, steps=60.

A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom is spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `longhand` AND NOT `result`. `result` is five clouds and no way to say they are the same hundred numbers, which is a picture of five sculptures rather than of an argument — the same objection noise_quarry and generator_bench both record. `longhand` is the only rung where this artifact's actual finding is legible without a caption: on the spread row the first three bars are the SAME BAR and the last two are not, so a visitor can see that chaos, noise and pattern do not narrow the draw at all and that only the last two rungs of the curriculum's ladder contract anything. A visitor who meets only the default meets the finding. `trace` is one token away and is the right value for a room that wants the five clouds and the carry to dominate.

WHY `60` AND NOT `0`. 60 is one second of the parent's own frame, and it is where all five stations are simultaneously legible: measured, the evolution knot is 1.64 simulation metres of spread at 60 (0.25 m displayed, 21 px) and 0.07 at 120, which is a body and a half and reads as an empty bay. Past ~90 steps the axis stops being a ladder of separation and becomes a ladder of one station vanishing. 0 is the value that proves the shared draw and it is kept, but as a rung and not as home: an arc whose five stations are five copies of one scatter is a proof, not an exhibit.

DECLARATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING TWICE OVER. `evidence` is listed first because build_dna_gallery.sweep walks the axes in declaration order and trims the LATER one from the tail of its value list until the cross product fits the cap; at the gallery's default --max=9 a 3 x 3 declaration fits EXACTLY and nothing is trimmed, so the full sheet needs no flag. Below that cap the tail of `steps` goes, and the value list is therefore declared [60, 0, 30] and not [0, 30, 60]: the measured closest pair on the axis is 60 <-> 30 (30.41% focus at longhand), so trimming to two drops one member of the closest pair and keeps both the default and the widest pair, which is what law 16 asks for. An ascending list would have dropped the default.
dna.was:
did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched.

WHAT IT IS FOR. `chapter` was declared six times and the five randomness names are one script behind five tokens: extreme_randomness carries the axis, and particle_randomness_pure / _perlin / _patterns / _emergent are four .tscn wrappers that pin forced_demo = 0/1/2/3 with display_time = 1e6, which is chapter = chaos / noise / pattern / emergence spelled as four artifacts. `evolution` has no wrapper and has never been placed anywhere in the corpus. So the family can show any ONE chapter, and the sixth value — the one that means all of them — is a ten-second timer that a still photograph cannot hold. This is the cross-member argument those six declarations leave unbuilt.

AND WHAT IT CORRECTS. extreme_randomness's registry says the five "differ in SILHOUETTE before they differ in anything else (a 10 m cube, a flat 20 x 5 panel, a disc, a 2 m ball, a 2 m line)", and it is right — but those silhouettes are STAGED, not earned. They are five different initial conditions written into start_demo's match block at :271-286 and applied before any update rule has run once. The parent's arc is therefore five systems that look different because they were built different, and a reader has no way to tell how much of the difference is the rule and how much is the staging. This arc hands all five the SAME hundred draws and lets only the rule separate them, which is what makes `steps = 0` worth photographing and what makes the census able to disagree with the curriculum. It does: it does not agree that the ladder is monotone.
dna.finding:
THE CURRICULUM'S LADDER IS NOT MONOTONE IN CONSTRAINT, and this is the first artifact that could measure it.

The five chapters are taught as five stages of one idea, each more constrained than the last. The census counts the spread of each station's reading — the rms distance of the hundred bodies from their own centre, in simulation metres, against one ceiling fixed across all nine frames — and at every value of `steps` the first three stations report the SAME NUMBER:

  steps=0    5.04  5.04  5.04  5.04  5.04     (the shared draw, before any rule)
  steps=30   5.04  5.04  5.05  4.76  3.48
  steps=60   5.06  5.09  5.08  4.19  1.64

THE FALSIFIABLE CLAIM, in the artifact's own gauge. On the spread row, bars 1, 2 and 3 are THE SAME BAR at every value of `steps`. At 13.35 px per simulation metre the predicted separation among them is 0.00 px at steps 0 (identical to the byte), 0.14 px at steps 30 and 0.42 px at steps 60. FALSIFYING THRESHOLD: 2 px. If any two of the first three spread bars differ by more than 2 px in any tile, this claim is wrong and the ladder does constrain from its first rung.

THE HEADROOM IS TIGHT ON PURPOSE, AND HERE IT IS. The nearest bar that is NOT a member of the equality is bar 4 at steps 30, which stands 3.7 px short of bar 1 — so at the axis's tightest rung the test separates a member from a non-member by a factor of 1.8, not by an order of magnitude. At steps 60, the default, it is comfortable: bar 4 is 11.6 px short of bar 1 and bar 5 is 45.6 px short. Three identical bars, then a step, then a collapse — visible in one still without a caption, which is why `longhand` is the default and why 60 is.

WHAT IT MEANS, stated carefully. It does not mean the first three chapters do nothing: noise bunches the draw onto the attracting sheets of its field and pattern bands it by radius, and both are plainly visible in the frame. It means they re-TEXTURE the draw without narrowing it, and that only the last two rungs — the two that read other bodies — contract anything. The word the curriculum uses is "constraint", and on the only measure this artifact can take, three of its five rungs apply none.
dna.kin:
FIVE OF THE SIX NAMES ARE ONE SCRIPT, WHICH IS THE CORPUS'S USUAL HIDDEN FAMILY IN ITS LARGEST FORM. extreme_randomness, particle_randomness_pure, particle_randomness_perlin, particle_randomness_patterns and particle_randomness_emergent all resolve to extrem_randomness.gd; the four wrappers each pin one chapter through the legacy `forced_demo` int and are deliberately left undeclared in the registry, because each token's NAME is its pinned value and an axis on them would let a map make particle_randomness_perlin show emergence. evolutionary_algorithms and particle_randomness_evolutionary are a sixth and seventh name on a SUBCLASS of the same file and declare `selection` instead, with a standing warning never to declare `chapter` on that scene.

THE OUTLIER, RECORDED AS THE BRIEF ASKS. facade_grammar_demo (registry/arrays.json) declares `chapter` with all | topology | organic | compound | decoration | bridge — an ARCHITECTURAL list over twenty mesh-grammar specimens, sharing with the randomness dialect only the word and the leading `all`. Its own dna.note says the word and the leading `all` are ITS, borrowed by extreme_randomness, "where 'all' likewise admits the whole book unfiltered". So the two dialects agree about exactly one thing — that `all` is the everything-at-once rung — and about nothing else, which is why this arc takes the randomness list and does not pretend the two are comparable. Note that the corpus disagrees elsewhere about what to call that slot: `regime` has three names for it (all in bifurcation_diagram / bifurcation_walkway / mass_spring_damper, free in control_pendulum / harmonic_motion_demo / rotation_gimbal, ringing in spring_demo) across artifacts that otherwise agree completely. `chapter` is the word whose two dialects agree about the slot and disagree about everything after it.

THE VALUE LIST IS NOT RETYPED. The five station names, their order and their count are read at build time out of CHAPTER_SRC.CHAPTER_DEMOS — extrem_randomness.gd:43, `const CHAPTER_DEMOS: PackedStringArray = ["chaos", "noise", "pattern", "emergence", "evolution"]` — and _check_family_list() push_errors in BOTH directions at _ready: a chapter the family declares that this arc has no station for, and a station this arc builds that the family has dropped. `all` is correctly absent from that const (the parent says so at :41-42), which is what lets the check be an exact set comparison rather than a subset one. ELITE_FRACTION is read from the same file, so the tenth that turns gold here is the tenth that turns gold there.

extrem_randomness.gd IS THE ONE PRELOADED, and it passes the same test noise_quarry and generator_bench applied to their families: it is the only member of the chapter family whose script parses with NO external dependency — no class_name, no preload, no reference to a global class. It is also the file whose five update rules this arc ports, so one preload does both jobs and the vocabulary cannot come apart from the implementation.

`evidence` is the family word of forty-eight registry names, taken character for character in the three-rung sub-list that noise_quarry, generator_bench, boundary_tank, ftc_bridge, zeno_staircase, sine_wave_controller and selection_garden carry. It is preloaded out of noise_quarry.gd's own EVIDENCES const, exactly as generator_bench does, so the three synthesis artifacts that share it cannot drift into three vocabularies.

`taxonomy` (table | ladder | stack | heap) WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, on the record, because it is the obvious second borrow: seven artifacts carry it including facade_grammar_demo, the sixth member of this very family, and it asks what ORDER a display claims its members have — which sounds like this arc's question. It is not. There the members are twenty finished specimens whose order is a curatorial claim, and `heap` withholds the captions to argue the classification was ours. Here the five stations are not laid out in an order at all: they are laid out in the order the SHARED DRAW passes through them, and the x coordinate is not a claim about ranking, it is the reading index. `stack` would put five clouds of a hundred bodies on one footprint, which is not a column of descriptions but an occlusion; `heap` would withhold the five chapter names, which are the exhibited family word and the one thing that must stand at every value. Borrowing the word while three of its four answers mean something else is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary.
dna.declines:
THE PARENT'S PER-BODY EMISSION, declined and COSTED rather than waved away. update_pure_random (:324-327) sets `material.emission = Color(speed*0.2, speed*0.1, speed*0.3)` with `emission_energy = speed * 0.5`, and _evolve_toward (:537-538) sets a flat gold emission at energy 0.5 on the winners. Each station here is ONE vertex-coloured mesh, which is what keeps five hundred bodies to five draw calls; a per-body emission needs a per-body material, and StandardMaterial3D has no per-vertex emission channel to bake it into.

WHAT THAT COSTS, measured and not guessed. At 60 steps the chaos station's mean body speed is 0.5254 and its fastest is 0.8854, so the parent's own emission_energy there runs 0.26 mean and 0.44 max — about a fifth of the 1.25 key at its brightest, not a rounding error. The chaos station in this artifact is therefore slightly darker and less violet than the same hundred bodies would be in extreme_randomness. It is declined anyway, for two reasons: baking it into the vertex ALBEDO would make an unlit term lit and would be a different picture wearing the same numbers (law 14), and the term is a function of SPEED, which is exactly the quantity a still cannot show. Stated here so that nobody reads the chaos station as evidence about the parent's brightness.

THE GOLD WINNERS' FLAT 0.5 EMISSION is declined with it, for consistency. The winners are already 1.6x the radius of a standard body (10.15 px against 6.35) and the only gold objects anywhere in the frame, so the mark survives the loss.

TIME. Every one of the five update rules reads Time.get_ticks_msec() — :331, :361, :401, :470 — and every one of them is frozen at t = 0 here. That is not a simplification, it is the only way a still can be deterministic (law 11), and it is stated because it changes two of the five in ways worth knowing: at t = 0 the noise field's third argument is 0, so the field has no z term left and is a 2D field extruded through z, and the evolution target is Vector3(3*sin 0, 2*cos 0, sin 0) = (0, 2, 0), a fixed point above the draw's centre rather than a moving optimum. evolutionary_algorithms records the same wall-clock problem from the other side and chose NOT to normalise it, because five live placements depend on the motion. This artifact has no placements to protect, so it freezes.

THE `selection` AXIS. extrem_randomness.gd carries a second declared axis, drift | uniform | culled | split, which reaches the evolution station's rule. It is not declared here: it would change ONE of five stations and leave four untouched, which is a local axis on a wide subject, and it is already swept on two tokens that pin that chapter. The arc runs at `culled`, the shipped pressure and the default of both tokens that declare the word.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels. tools/artifact_dna_critic.py crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers below come from building this exact geometry in Python — the same five ported rules, THE SAME HUNDRED BODIES (see below), the same layout constants, the same census — rasterising it with a z-buffer at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.60) and pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE DRAW IS THE SAME DRAW, not a statistically similar one. The generator is a 32-bit LCG written out in the script (multiplier 1664525, increment 1013904223, eight warm-up draws, station streams seeded SEED + i * 2654435761) rather than RandomNumberGenerator, precisely so that the replica draws the identical hundred positions, velocities and colours in the identical order. That is the difference between predicting this artifact and predicting an artifact like it.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `steps` 60 <-> 30, AT evidence=longhand: 30.41% focus, 1.91% frame. It clears the critic's TWIN_FOCUS bar of 6.00% by 24.4 points, so I predict NO twins anywhere on the sheet — the smallest number in the whole 3 x 3 is 23.91% (result <-> trace at steps 0) and the WEAK bar is 12%.

WHY THAT PAIR, AND IT IS NOT THE REASON I FIRST WROTE DOWN. The obvious answer is that 30 and 60 are nearer each other than either is to 0, and the arithmetic says that is FALSE. Mean per-body displacement between readings, in simulation metres:
    30 <-> 60   chaos 0.30   noise 0.49   pattern 0.60   emergence 0.58   evolution 2.17
     0 <-> 30   chaos 0.42   noise 0.49   pattern 0.60   emergence 0.42   evolution 1.68
     0 <-> 60   chaos 0.72   noise 0.96   pattern 1.19   emergence 0.94   evolution 3.81
30 <-> 60 is the SMALLER gap at only one station of five, equal at two, and larger at two. In pure displacement it is not the closest pair at all.

The real reason is the COLOUR LAWS, and it is a fact about where they live. Every one of the five is set inside an update_* function, and start_demo (:292-293) resets albedo to the colour the body was drawn with, so at zero applications no station has a colour law and all five wear the draw's own random colours. steps = 0 is therefore the only rung at which four of the five stations are painted differently from every other rung — noise's positional sinusoids, pattern's angular bands, emergence's radial rings and evolution's gold-and-ramp are all absent. Any pair involving 0 carries a whole-station repaint at four stations on top of whatever moved; 60 <-> 30 is the only pair on the axis where the five stations differ by POSITION ALONE. That is worth 5 to 10 points of focus, and it is why the closest pair is the one the displacement table says it should not be.

THE WHOLE PREDICTED SHEET, frame% / focus%.
  `evidence`, at each steps rung:
    result <-> trace      @ 60  1.85 / 33.37     @ 0  1.22 / 23.91     @ 30  1.55 / 28.85
    result <-> longhand   @ 60  4.78 / 51.53     @ 0  4.06 / 44.47     @ 30  4.42 / 47.78
    trace  <-> longhand   @ 60  3.28 / 43.68     @ 0  3.08 / 39.87     @ 30  3.18 / 41.68
  `steps`, at each evidence rung:
    60 <-> 0    @ result 3.33 / 44.09    @ trace 3.16 / 42.01    @ longhand 3.03 / 42.11
    60 <-> 30   @ result 2.19 / 33.10    @ trace 2.06 / 30.73    @ longhand 1.91 / 30.41
    0  <-> 30   @ result 2.90 / 40.02    @ trace 2.75 / 38.25    @ longhand 2.41 / 36.32
  AXIS MEANS: `evidence` 3.05% frame / 39.46% focus -> BITES. `steps` 2.64% / 37.45% -> BITES.
  Subject fraction of frame at the default tile: 8.74%. Crop at (longhand, 30): 582 x 262 px.

THE LOWER-BOUND RULE, AND THE ONE PLACE THIS ARTIFACT MAY BREAK IT. doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md records four predictions that each under-shot by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a Python rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading and no shadows, AO or antialiasing. Every one of those four was a SOLID subject. This one is not: it is five clouds of a hundred 6 px bodies, and on a speckle field antialiasing works in the opposite direction — it softens the very edges the difference metric is reading, and the real render has MSAA and a shadow pass the replica does not. So the usual "measured must exceed predicted" reading is NOT safe here and is not claimed. What is claimed instead is a hard floor, and it is the thing to check:

  IF THE CLOSEST PAIR (steps 60 <-> 30 at longhand) COMES BACK UNDER 12% FOCUS, OR IF ANY
  PAIR ON THE SHEET COMES BACK UNDER 6%, SOMETHING IS BROKEN — and the first thing to check
  is not the design but whether _step_* mutated the caller's array (see dna.fixture_note).

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT DISAGREED. The first design for the origin datum was a twelve-edge cage around each station's draw box. Rasterised: at 0.75 m a side its screen-x extent is 1.046 m against a station pitch of 1.172 m, so neighbouring cages OVERLAPPED by 0.065 m, and the cyan was the single loudest thing in every frame — furniture in front of the marks, law 7 exactly, and it was inflating `evidence` to 52.56% focus on its own scaffolding. It was replaced by four rails on the floor of the box plus four short corner posts, which say the same thing under the bodies instead of around them, and the pitch was opened from 1.34 m to 1.60 m. Worst measured neighbour gap now 9.4 px, at chaos <-> noise at steps 0.

AND ONE BUG CAUGHT ON PAPER RATHER THAN ON SCREEN, which is the only way this pass could catch it, since it is forbidden to run Godot. The carry ribbon's face normal was written as cross(b0 - a0, a1 - a0) * -1.0, and working the prism out by hand for an axis along +x shows that is INWARD: u = d x up = (0,0,1) and w = d x u = (0,-1,0), so off[0] = (0,-h,+h) and off[1] = (0,+h,+h) both sit at z = +h and that quad IS the +z face, whose outward normal is the UN-negated cross. Every carry ribbon would have been lit by the 0.55 ambient alone, with no key and no fill, on the one mark that carries this artifact's thesis. Fixed in the script and in the replica, and the sheet above is measured after the fix: it moved result <-> trace at steps 60 from 31.87% to 33.37% focus, which is 1.5 points of the `evidence` axis that were being thrown away.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL NINE FRAMES, which is also the box at seven of the nine. Union 7.70 x 1.72 x 1.215 — x across the five bays plus the apron's 0.12 m margins, y from the apron underside to the board top, z from the board's back face to the apron's front edge. Diagonal sqrt(59.29 + 2.9584 + 1.476225) = 7.982772, radius 3.991386. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 3.991386 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 24.805 m and show a 15.167 m frame around a 7.70 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding radius, which is why a long apron object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.60 the camera comes to 14.8830 m and the frame to 9.1004 m, which is 83.51 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting the subject's measured bounding box at the default tile is 582 x 262 px of the 760 x 760 frame, with 121 px of margin on the left and 57 px on the right, covering 8.74% of the frame. The margins are not equal and the reason is perspective, not an error: the camera stands on the +x/+z side, so the +x end of a 7.70 m apron is nearer and projects further out. 0.57 was measured too and leaves only 38 px on the right, which is less slack than a showcase key light's specular fringe the replica does not model; 0.63 costs 0.6 points of subject fraction and 4 px off every mark for nothing. Cropping is arithmetically impossible above framing = 1 / PAD = 0.5263 because the rig fits by bounding SPHERE, so 0.60 keeps 14% of sphere margin in hand on top of the 57 measured pixels.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: it makes almost no difference and that is worth stating rather than assuming. The apron (7.70 x 1.215 at the base) and the board (y 1.32 to 1.72) define five of the six faces at evidence=longhand and neither moves with either axis. At result and trace there is no board, so the box is 1.32 m tall instead of 1.72 and the camera would come in — the sweep's fixed_camera path takes the union, which is correct, and all nine tiles are framed identically. The bodies live inside the apron's z envelope at every rung (measured -0.445 to +0.407 against the apron's -0.58 to +0.58) and under the board's lower edge (tallest body top 1.172 against 1.32), so nothing the axes move can reach a bound.

THE SMALLEST MARK IN THE ARTIFACT IS 2.5 px AND IT IS DELIBERATE. The pattern station carries the parent's own radius law (:397), radius = 0.05 + 0.03 * sin(2d), so its smallest body is 0.4 of the ratio-1 size: 2.54 px against the standard 6.35. Compressing that law to keep every body above 3 px would be redrawing the parent's arithmetic to flatter the bench, which is law 14 — the pattern station's size banding is a true reading of the rule and the small bodies are the trough of it. Every mark that either AXIS moves is above 3.6 px.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE IS NEEDED AND NO SEED EXPORT IS OFFERED. The draw is seeded from a constant (SEED_BASE = 20260813) through an LCG written out in the file, so every boot on every machine builds the same hundred bodies; there is no randf(), no randomize(), no RandomNumberGenerator, no _process, no timer and no physics anywhere in the artifact, and every one of the five rules reads its time argument as a literal 0. A seed export was deliberately NOT added: a synthesis whose whole claim is that five stations share ONE draw should not offer a knob that changes which draw, because the only thing it could vary is the thing that must not vary between the five.

THE ONE TRAP THIS BUILD ALREADY WALKED INTO, recorded because it fails silently. The five rules take the working state as an argument and mutate it. Written with PackedVector3Array — the obvious type for a hundred positions — that does nothing at all: Godot 4 packed arrays are copy-on-write VALUE types, so each _step_* would have written to its own copy and every station would have returned its draw unmoved, at every value of `steps`, with no error, no warning and a sheet of nine frames showing five identical scatters. The state is Array[Vector3] throughout for that reason, and the comment in the file says so. If a future edit changes it back, the tell is `steps` reading INERT while `evidence` still bites.

THE BUILD COST IS PAID ONCE PER `steps` VALUE, NOT PER AXIS VALUE. _read_stations() caches on `steps` and returns immediately when it has not changed, so switching `evidence` adds and removes marks without re-running a single step. The emergence station is the expensive one — it is O(n^2) in the hundred bodies, 60 times — and its separation test is the parent's `dist < 0.5` written on the SQUARE so the sqrt is paid only by near pairs: identical branch, and the difference between a build under a tenth of a second and one over a second.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `evidence`, by construction: the apron, the five bays, the five chapter tabs and all five station clouds. Everything that changes between the three tiles is proof apparatus — the origin frames, the carry ribbons, the board and its ten bars — which is the axis's whole subject.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `steps`: the apron, the bays, the tabs, the board, its tonal step, the ten bar POSITIONS and both census ceilings. The origin frames are constant too, and that is the sharper claim: they mark the shared draw, and the draw does not move. So the only step-dependent part of the result -> trace delta is the carry ribbons, and result <-> trace must therefore RISE MONOTONICALLY with steps as the ribbons lengthen. Predicted 23.91 (steps 0) -> 28.85 (30) -> 33.37 (60). If it does not rise monotonically, the ribbons are not being drawn from the trajectory the bodies actually took.

THE FIVE STATIONS ARE NOT MEANT TO LOOK EQUALLY DIFFERENT. chaos, noise and pattern are the closest three at every rung and that is correct — see dna.finding, which is what the census exists to say out loud. If a viewer reports that the leftmost three clouds "look the same", that is the artifact working.

THE ARTIFACT'S OWN DARK SPOT, DRAWN RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The census can see the two things the eye cannot measure — spread and carry — and it is blind to the thing the eye sees instantly, which is STRUCTURE. noise's cloud bunches onto the field's attracting sheets and pattern's bands by radius, and both readings have the same rms spread as chaos to two decimal places. The census says the ladder is not monotone in EXTENT; it says nothing at all about whether the ladder is monotone in ORDER, and this artifact does not measure that. Stated so that the three equal bars are not over-read.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE. There are five Label3D in the artifact and they letter the five chapters — chaos, noise, pattern, emergence, evolution — which are present at every value of both axes. Not one pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own variant. Billboard is off, which also keeps LabelFramer out: it treats billboard-enabled as the hanging signal and would bolt a panel and a bezel behind each tab.

A NOTE FOR WHOEVER MEASURES THIS SHEET, because it cost a measurement to find. THE CRITIC'S CURRENCY CANNOT VERIFY AN IDENTITY ON A SPARSE SUBJECT. At steps = 0 the five stations hold the same hundred bodies at the same coordinates in the same colours — identical to the byte, offset only by 1.60 m of x — and cropping the five stations out of that one frame and comparing neighbours in the critic's own pipeline gives 48.98% mean focus (worst 50.79). It is not a fault in the artifact: 1.60 m of parallax across a field of a hundred 6 px bodies decorrelates the hottest 5% of pixels completely. The identity DOES show, but only as a drop — 48.98% at steps 0 against 64.01% at steps 30 — and never as a zero. Any reading of this sheet that expects a sparse subject to produce small numbers for small differences will be wrong in the same way.
